elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Any such audit shall be permitted no more than once in any 12-month period..." — express frequency cap replacing the previously unlimited request right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "...and upon at least 30 days' written notice from Licensor." The prior sentence ("permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request"), which was a compliance deadline on Licensee rather than notice, was replaced so no contradictory retained text remains.
Inserted: "...during business hours..." in the same operative sentence.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Retained original: "an independent Certified Public Accountant or other Audit Professional, (selected by mutual agreement)" — independence plus mutual selection; no edit required.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "by an auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations".

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Each such audit shall be conducted off-site where possible..." — tracks the checklist wording including the "where possible" qualifier.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained p0064: "The cost of the audit will be borne by Licensor unless a discrepancy of more than five-percent (5%) is discovered, in which case the cost of the audit shall be borne by Licensee." Vendor (Licensor) is the default cost bearer with a 5% shift trigger.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "and Licensor shall have no direct access to Licensee's systems." The clause is otherwise limited to "accounting records", so no retained sentence contradicts this.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: "no more than once in any 12-month period" satisfies the annual cap.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: 30 days' written notice exceeds the 15-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained cost sentence places cost on Licensor with a 5% shift threshold, which the playbook ranks as the preferred (stronger) position over the 10% fallback threshold; the cost-allocation direction required by the element is satisfied.

reasons: All eight preferred elements are met in operative language: the inserted sentence supplies frequency (once per 12 months), 30 days' written notice and business-hours limits; the second inserted sentence supplies off-site-where-possible conduct, a confidentiality-bound auditor and an express no-direct-system-access bar; and the existing independent CPA/Audit Professional selection and Licensor-borne cost with 5% shift are retained untouched.

Minimality holds: the only deleted words are the original "Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor" sentence, whose removal is necessary because a Licensee-side 30-day compliance deadline would otherwise contradict the new 30-days'-advance-notice requirement. No survival tails, expense allocations, procedures or extra remedies were added; the additions map one-to-one onto checklist elements.

Intent preserved: the scope of the audit ("appropriate accounting records to ensure compliance with all terms of this Agreement"), the mutual-agreement auditor selection and the p0064 cost-shifting mechanic all survive without contradiction, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Finding status "deviation" is supportable: pre-redline the clause had no frequency cap and no advance notice, failing both fallback elements on those points and approaching the unlimited-audit walk-away.
Minor drafting note (not a defect): the retained cost sentence uses "discrepancy" rather than "underpayment"; it is favourable existing language and correctly left unamended.
